stem: A test has 1 primary metric named in advance and 8 secondary metrics shown for context. Which way of reading them avoids the multiple-testing trap?

options.text: Ship if any of the 9 metrics shows p < 0.05, since each one was measured
Pick the primary metric after the test, choosing the one that moved most
Average the 9 p-values and ship if that average falls below 0.05
Decide on the primary metric; treat secondary wins as hypotheses
